correctness.rationale: Kummer and Legendre turn the claim into two directly checked ternary-digit carry statistics. Each of six state/digit transitions is derived, the 2x2 matrix gives the exact generating function by Cayley–Hamilton, and explicit digit words prove the support. The carry Markov contraction rigorously gives exact finite-depth moments; simple analytic spectral perturbation gives the bivariate Gaussian limit with zero mixed limiting cumulant. Exact-arithmetic independent enumerations through \(3^9\) and actual integer binomials corroborate, not replace, the all-depth proof.

originality.rationale: The novel claim is the case-specific all-depth joint bivariate valuation polynomial, exact attainable pairs, order-one positive covariance and independent Gaussian limit. The classical Kummer/Legendre product identity and generic finite-matrix method are not claimed as new. Examined published full/partial primary texts deal with row-wise valuation distributions or different generalized coefficients; their stated results do not contain or immediately imply the same-index joint census. value.rationale: A natural factorization produces the known sum of two prime valuations but provides no full simultaneous divisibility law. The new exact bivariate polynomial and complete support turn that gap into an unrestricted classification for all lengths. A nontrivial distinction emerges between positive finite-depth correlation and independent Gaussian fluctuations, with explicit bounded covariance, exact means and variances. The result is structural rather than a few computed cases.
